items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: she had a nice voice in the style of Ella Fitzgerald

ctx.x: Floyd Smith was well known for his 'Floyd's Guitar Blues' which he did on a table type Hawaiian guitar, and he was quite a funky guitar player on other numbers. Booker Collins was a solid bass man with a very nice charactar and Ben Thigpen was a nice drummer.

June Richmond had been in the show at the Harlem Club where the Benny Carter band had played in 1933 and I had seen her later at the Lafayette Theatre. June was quite heavy and must have weighed more than Big Jim although she was just a little taller than Shorty Baker. But she didn't need a microphone or loud speakers to be heard when she sang. June had a voice like an opera singer, but she could swing a number like Ella Fitzgerald and the band didn't have to play soft for her. She also did comical numbers and…
The first date I did with the Band was at the Howard Theatre in Washington, and as we were obliged to rehearse the show as soon as we arrived, I didn't know any of the band members.
